text: Four things in every Tableau view need formatting sooner or later: numbers, dates, axes, and headers. All four go through the same place — the Format pane.

Right-click any number in the view and choose Format. The Numbers dropdown offers Automatic, Number, Currency, Scientific, and Percentage — each with Standard and Custom variants. Pick Currency (Standard), choose a locale, and every value in that field displays with the right symbol and decimal convention.

Dates work the same way — right-click a date field and choose Format. Tableau gives you a list of common presets, and for continuous or exact discrete dates, a Custom option using format symbols you combine yourself, like day, month abbreviation, and year.

Axes are what a continuous field renders as — and they can be formatted just like any other number. Here, the Sales axis on this stacked column chart is formatted as currency, so every gridline value reads as a dollar amount instead of a raw number.

Headers are what a discrete field renders as — the row and column labels showing each member's name. This view's column headers show Order Date broken into years, and its row headers show each Sub-Category, both fully controllable through the same right-click Format menu.
Next lesson, you'll add titles, captions, reference lines, and annotations — the layer of context that turns a chart into something a reader can actually interpret without you standing next to them.
